message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 331, "amount_cents": 2690}, {"order_id": 332, "amount_cents": 1286}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds on record.
The ledger's refunds (331 and 332, with matching amounts) match Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I need the orders to find which customers to pay.

The ledger's refunds (331 for 2690 and 332 for 1286) match Alpha's handoff. The orders cover three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net_balance (43101) equals its orders 330 + 333 (20999 + 22102) with no refunds against it, and both ledger refunds match Alpha's handoff. Alpha's refund work checks out, so I can pay Acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get Birch's net balance; Birch has order 331 (refunded 2690) and order 334, so I'll check the figure against that before paying.

Birch's orders are 331 (7475) and 334 (29770), totaling 37245. Subtracting the ledger refund for 331 (2690) gives 34555, which matches net_balance. Alpha's refunds still check out, so I'll record Birch's payout.
Acme and Birch are paid. The last customer is Cobalt, with order 332 (3119, refunded 1286) and order 335 (26850). I'll get Cobalt's net balance before paying.

Cobalt's orders total 29969 (332 at 3119 plus 335 at 26850). Subtracting the ledger refund for 332 (1286) gives 28683, which matches net_balance. Alpha's refunds check out for every customer, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three customers have been paid. Acme, Birch, and Cobalt each match their order totals minus ledger refunds, and Alpha's refunds 331 and 332 match the handoff. Reporting the payouts.
